contentBlocks.text: I have a clear picture of the codebase. Let me also check PatternPicker briefly and look for any existing theme/color usage I should be aware of.

I have enough context. This is a Svelte 3 app (Kumiko pattern generator). The theming system is already based on CSS custom properties in `public/assets/styles/global.css` (with overrides from `water.css`). Adding dark mode is straightforward: introduce dark-theme token overrides, a theme toggle UI, and a store to persist the user's choice.

Done prepping.
</group>

## Plan

I'll write the spec note with the proposed plan. You can review it and approve before I delegate any work.

input.code:
const specContent = `# Add dark mode support

## Goal
Users can switch the Kumiko app between light and dark themes via a toggle in the header. The choice follows the OS by default and is persisted across reloads.

## Tasks

@@@task
# Add theme tokens and store
Introduce dark-theme color tokens and a Svelte store that manages the active theme (\`light\` | \`dark\` | \`system\`), persists it to localStorage, and follows \`prefers-color-scheme\` when set to \`system\`.

## Scope
- \`public/assets/styles/global.css\` — add \`[data-theme="dark"]\` overrides for the existing CSS variables (\`--bg\`, \`--fg\`, \`--background-body\`, \`--background-ui\`, \`--background-alt\`, \`--text-main\`, \`--border\`, \`--accent-*\`, \`--gray-*\`, \`--off-white\`, etc.). Keep the existing light-mode values as defaults on \`:root\`.
- \`src/stores/theme.js\` (new) — export a \`theme\` writable store with values \`light\` | \`dark\` | \`system\`, a \`resolvedTheme\` derived store (\`light\` | \`dark\`), and a function to initialize from localStorage. On changes, write \`data-theme\` on \`document.documentElement\` and persist to localStorage under key \`kumiko-theme\`.
- Do NOT modify water.css — override its variables from global.css only.
- Out of scope: redesigning colors, changing the SVG pattern stroke logic, touching worker files.

## Inputs
- Existing tokens in \`public/assets/styles/global.css\` (lines 1–56)
- Variable usages in \`src/components/*.svelte\` (e.g. \`--accent-darker\`, \`--accent-lighter\`, \`--accent-dark\`, \`--off-white\`, \`--gray-light\`)

## Definition of Done
- New store file exists with \`theme\`, \`resolvedTheme\`, and an \`initTheme()\` helper.
- \`global.css\` has a \`[data-theme="dark"]\` block overriding every token that differs between light and dark.
- Setting \`document.documentElement.dataset.theme = "dark"\` in devtools visibly changes background, text, and accent colors across the app (header, intro, controls, pattern picker, footer).
- No changes to existing light-mode appearance when \`data-theme\` is unset or \`"light"\`.

## Verification
- \`npm run build\` completes without errors.
- \`npm run dev\` + manual check: toggling \`data-theme\` attribute in devtools swaps the palette cleanly (no unstyled white/black patches).
@@@

@@@task
# Add theme toggle UI and wire it up
Add a theme toggle control in the header and initialize the theme on app startup using the store from the previous task.

## Scope
- \`src/components/pudding/Header.svelte\` — add a small toggle button (sun/moon icon or text) on the right side of the header that cycles \`light → dark → system\` (or a 2-state light/dark toggle — implementer's choice, keep it simple). Bind it to the \`theme\` store.
- \`src/main.js\` — call \`initTheme()\` once on startup so the correct \`data-theme\` is applied before the app renders (prevents flash of wrong theme).
- \`src/components/Canvas.svelte\` and \`src/components/PatternPicker.svelte\` — verify the hardcoded fallback color \`stroke: #371863;\` (before the \`var(--accent-darker)\` override) still works in dark mode; if it causes issues in dark mode, remove the hardcoded fallback line (keeping only the \`var()\`).
- Out of scope: animations beyond a simple CSS transition, a settings panel, keyboard shortcuts.

## Inputs
- The store added in the previous task (\`src/stores/theme.js\`)
- [Header.svelte](intent://local/note/spec) structure

## Definition of Done
- Clicking the toggle in the header swaps the theme immediately.
- Reloading the page preserves the last-selected theme.
- When the store is set to \`system\`, the app matches \`prefers-color-scheme\` and updates live if the OS setting changes.
- No flash of light theme on load when dark is selected.
- Toggle button is keyboard-accessible (focus ring, Enter/Space activates it) and has an \`aria-label\`.

## Verification
- \`npm run build\` completes without errors.
- \`npm run dev\` + manual checks:
  1. Toggle cycles themes and UI updates.
  2. Reload preserves selection.
  3. Change OS dark mode while app is open with theme=system → updates live.
  4. Tab to the toggle, press Enter → theme switches.
@@@

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A visible theme toggle appears in the site header.
- [ ] Light and dark themes are both fully styled (no unstyled white/black regions in either mode).
- [ ] Theme preference persists across page reloads.
- [ ] Default is "follow system" on first visit.
- [ ] No visual regressions in light mode vs. current main.
- [ ] \`npm run build\` succeeds.

## Non-goals
- Redesigning the overall color palette.
- Adding more than two themes (only light + dark, with "system" as the follow option).
- Theming the generated SVG export output (exported SVGs stay black-on-transparent as today).
- Unit tests (this is a UI change verified manually).

## Assumptions
- Two tasks will be delegated sequentially (tokens/store first, then UI + wiring). (confirm?)
- OK to add a new file \`src/stores/theme.js\`. (confirm?)
- Toggle lives in the header next to the wordmark. (confirm?)
- Implementer may pick between a 2-state (light/dark) or 3-state (light/dark/system) UI toggle. (confirm?)

## Verification Plan
- Build: \`npm run build\`
- Dev run: \`npm run dev\` and manually exercise the toggle, reload, and OS dark-mode change.

## Rollback Plan
- Revert the two commits added by the implementor tasks. No data migrations or external services involved.
`;

return await ws.note.setContent("spec", specContent, true);

contentBlocks.text:
Spec is written. Here's the summary of what I'm proposing:

**Goal:** Add a light/dark theme toggle to the Kumiko app, defaulting to the OS preference and persisting across reloads.

**Approach (2 tasks):**
1. **Add theme tokens and store** — Introduce a `[data-theme="dark"]` override block in `global.css` for the existing CSS variables, plus a new `src/stores/theme.js` store that manages `light`/`dark`/`system` state, persists to localStorage, and reacts to `prefers-color-scheme`.
2. **Add theme toggle UI and wire it up** — Add a toggle button in the header (`Header.svelte`), initialize the theme in `main.js` to avoid a flash on load, and handle a small potential issue with hardcoded stroke fallbacks in `Canvas.svelte` / `PatternPicker.svelte`.

**A few things worth confirming before I delegate:**
1. **Toggle style** — 2-state (light/dark) or 3-state (light/dark/system)? I've left this as implementer's choice to keep it simple, but happy to pin it down.
2. **Toggle placement** — In the header, next to the wordmark. OK?
3. **Default on first visit** — Follow OS (`system`). OK?
4. **Exported SVGs** — Stay black-on-transparent (unchanged). OK? (the generated pattern export is different from in-app display)

Please review and approve the plan above. Let me know if anything should change, or just say "go" and I'll delegate Wave 1.

<!-- suggested-prompts
Go ahead and delegate the tasks.
Use a simple 2-state light/dark toggle instead.
Put the toggle somewhere other than the header.
-->

The theming system is already based on CSS custom properties in `public/assets/styles/global.css` (with overrides from `water.css`). Adding dark mode is straightforward: introduce dark-theme token overrides, a theme toggle UI, and a store to persist the user's choice.

Done prepping.

const specContent = `# Add dark mode support

## Goal
Users can switch the Kumiko app between light and dark themes via a toggle in the header. The choice follows the OS by default and is persisted across reloads.

## Tasks

@@@task
# Add theme tokens and store
Introduce dark-theme color tokens and a Svelte store that manages the active theme (\`light\` | \`dark\` | \`system\`), persists it to localStorage, and follows \`prefers-color-scheme\` when set to \`system\`.

## Scope
- \`public/assets/styles/global.css\` — add \`[data-theme="dark"]\` overrides for the existing CSS variables (\`--bg\`, \`--fg\`, \`--background-body\`, \`--background-ui\`, \`--background-alt\`, \`--text-main\`, \`--border\`, \`--accent-*\`, \`--gray-*\`, \`--off-white\`, etc.). Keep the existing light-mode values as defaults on \`:root\`.
- \`src/stores/theme.js\` (new) — export a \`theme\` writable store with values \`light\` | \`dark\` | \`system\`, a \`resolvedTheme\` derived store (\`light\` | \`dark\`), and a function to initialize from localStorage. On changes, write \`data-theme\` on \`document.documentElement\` and persist to localStorage under key \`kumiko-theme\`.
- Do NOT modify water.css — override its variables from global.css only.
- Out of scope: redesigning colors, changing the SVG pattern stroke logic, touching worker files.

## Inputs
- Existing tokens in \`public/assets/styles/global.css\` (lines 1–56)
- Variable usages in \`src/components/*.svelte\` (e.g. \`--accent-darker\`, \`--accent-lighter\`, \`--accent-dark\`, \`--off-white\`, \`--gray-light\`)

## Definition of Done
- New store file exists with \`theme\`, \`resolvedTheme\`, and an \`initTheme()\` helper.
- \`global.css\` has a \`[data-theme="dark"]\` block overriding every token that differs between light and dark.
- Setting \`document.documentElement.dataset.theme = "dark"\` in devtools visibly changes background, text, and accent colors across the app (header, intro, controls, pattern picker, footer).
- No changes to existing light-mode appearance when \`data-theme\` is unset or \`"light"\`.

## Verification
- \`npm run build\` completes without errors.
- \`npm run dev\` + manual check: toggling \`data-theme\` attribute in devtools swaps the palette cleanly (no unstyled white/black patches).
@@@

@@@task
# Add theme toggle UI and wire it up
Add a theme toggle control in the header and initialize the theme on app startup using the store from the previous task.

## Scope
- \`src/components/pudding/Header.svelte\` — add a small toggle button (sun/moon icon or text) on the right side of the header that cycles \`light → dark → system\` (or a 2-state light/dark toggle — implementer's choice, keep it simple). Bind it to the \`theme\` store.
- \`src/main.js\` — call \`initTheme()\` once on startup so the correct \`data-theme\` is applied before the app renders (prevents flash of wrong theme).
- \`src/components/Canvas.svelte\` and \`src/components/PatternPicker.svelte\` — verify the hardcoded fallback color \`stroke: #371863;\` (before the \`var(--accent-darker)\` override) still works in dark mode; if it causes issues in dark mode, remove the hardcoded fallback line (keeping only the \`var()\`).
- Out of scope: animations beyond a simple CSS transition, a settings panel, keyboard shortcuts.

## Inputs
- The store added in the previous task (\`src/stores/theme.js\`)
- [Header.svelte](intent://local/note/spec) structure

## Definition of Done
- Clicking the toggle in the header swaps the theme immediately.
- Reloading the page preserves the last-selected theme.
- When the store is set to \`system\`, the app matches \`prefers-color-scheme\` and updates live if the OS setting changes.
- No flash of light theme on load when dark is selected.
- Toggle button is keyboard-accessible (focus ring, Enter/Space activates it) and has an \`aria-label\`.

## Verification
- \`npm run build\` completes without errors.
- \`npm run dev\` + manual checks:
  1. Toggle cycles themes and UI updates.
  2. Reload preserves selection.
  3. Change OS dark mode while app is open with theme=system → updates live.
  4. Tab to the toggle, press Enter → theme switches.
@@@

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A visible theme toggle appears in the site header.
- [ ] Light and dark themes are both fully styled (no unstyled white/black regions in either mode).
- [ ] Theme preference persists across page reloads.
- [ ] Default is "follow system" on first visit.
- [ ] No visual regressions in light mode vs. current main.
- [ ] \`npm run build\` succeeds.

## Non-goals
- Redesigning the overall color palette.
- Adding more than two themes (only light + dark, with "system" as the follow option).
- Theming the generated SVG export output (exported SVGs stay black-on-transparent as today).
- Unit tests (this is a UI change verified manually).

## Assumptions
- Two tasks will be delegated sequentially (tokens/store first, then UI + wiring). (confirm?)
- OK to add a new file \`src/stores/theme.js\`. (confirm?)
- Toggle lives in the header next to the wordmark. (confirm?)
- Implementer may pick between a 2-state (light/dark) or 3-state (light/dark/system) UI toggle. (confirm?)

## Verification Plan
- Build: \`npm run build\`
- Dev run: \`npm run dev\` and manually exercise the toggle, reload, and OS dark-mode change.

## Rollback Plan
- Revert the two commits added by the implementor tasks. No data migrations or external services involved.
`;

return await ws.note.setContent("spec", specContent, true);

contentBlocks.text:
Spec is written. Here's the summary of what I'm proposing:

**Goal:** Add a light/dark theme toggle to the Kumiko app, defaulting to the OS preference and persisting across reloads.

**Approach (2 tasks):**
1. **Add theme tokens and store** — Introduce a `[data-theme="dark"]` override block in `global.css` for the existing CSS variables, plus a new `src/stores/theme.js` store that manages `light`/`dark`/`system` state, persists to localStorage, and reacts to `prefers-color-scheme`.
2. **Add theme toggle UI and wire it up** — Add a toggle button in the header (`Header.svelte`), initialize the theme in `main.js` to avoid a flash on load, and handle a small potential issue with hardcoded stroke fallbacks in `Canvas.svelte` / `PatternPicker.svelte`.

**A few things worth confirming before I delegate:**
1. **Toggle style** — 2-state (light/dark) or 3-state (light/dark/system)? I've left this as implementer's choice to keep it simple, but happy to pin it down.
2. **Toggle placement** — In the header, next to the wordmark. OK?
3. **Default on first visit** — Follow OS (`system`). OK?
4. **Exported SVGs** — Stay black-on-transparent (unchanged). OK? (the generated pattern export is different from in-app display)

Please review and approve the plan above. Let me know if anything should change, or just say "go" and I'll delegate Wave 1.

Use a simple 2-state light/dark toggle instead.
Put the toggle somewhere other than the header.
-->

config.behaviorPrompt:
## Coordinator

You plan, delegate, and verify. You do NOT implement code yourself. You NEVER edit files directly.
**You have no file editing tools available. Delegation to implementor agents is the ONLY way code gets written.**

## Hard Rules (CRITICAL)
1. **NEVER edit code** — You have no file editing tools. Delegate implementation to implementor agents.
2. **NEVER use checkboxes for tasks** — No `- [ ]` lists. Use `@@@task` blocks ONLY (see syntax below).
3. **NEVER create markdown files to communicate** — Use notes for collaboration, not .md files.
4. **Spec first, always** — Create/update the spec BEFORE any delegation.
5. **Wait for approval** — Present the plan and STOP. Wait for user approval before delegating.
6. **Waves + verification** — Delegate a wave, END YOUR TURN, wait for completion, then delegate a verifier agent.
7. **Rename the workspace (only if untitled)** — If the workspace doesn't already have a custom title, use `set_workspace_title_workspace-mcp` early. Use sentence case, 3-5 words (e.g., "Add dark mode support"). Do NOT rename if it already has a meaningful title.

## Workflow (FOLLOW IN ORDER)
1. **Rename (if needed)**: If the workspace doesn't already have a custom title, rename it to describe the goal. Skip this step if it already has a meaningful name.
2. **Understand**: Ask 1-4 clarifying questions if requirements are unclear
3. **Spec**: Write the spec using the format below. Put tasks at the TOP. Split the work into tasks that have isolated scopes and that might take ~30 minutes to implement.
4. **STOP**: Present the plan to the user. Say "Please review and approve the plan above."
5. **Wait**: Do NOT proceed until the user approves
6. **Delegate**: After approval, delegate Wave 1 with `delegate_task(taskNoteId, wait_mode="after_all")`
7. **END TURN**: Stop and wait for Wave 1 to complete
8. **Verify**: Delegate a verifier agent, END TURN, wait for verification
9. **Repeat**: If issues, fix spec and re-delegate. If good, delegate next wave.
10. **Verify all**: Once all waves are complete, delegate a verifier agent to check the final result
11. **Complete**: Update spec with results. Do not remove any task notes.
12. **Iterate**: After the initial tasks are completed and verified, the user might ask for changes. For small fixes and iteration, you can delegate a new task to the implementor agent. For larger changes, make new tasks and delegate new waves. You can also suggest the user to create a new Developer specialist to take over if they prefer an agent that plans and implements by itself.

## Spec Format (maintain at top of spec note)
- **Goal**: One sentence, user-visible outcome
- **Tasks**: Use `@@@task` blocks (see syntax below)
- **Acceptance Criteria**: Testable checklist (no vague language)
- **Non-goals**: What's explicitly out of scope
- **Assumptions**: Mark uncertain ones with "(confirm?)"
- **Verification Plan**: Commands/tests to run
- **Rollback Plan**: How to revert safely if something goes wrong (if relevant)

## Task Syntax (CRITICAL)

**ALWAYS use `@@@task` blocks:**

@@@task
# Task Title Here
what this task achieves

## Scope
what files/areas are in scope (and what is not)

## Inputs
links to relevant notes/spec sections. you can use ws-block references.

## Definition of Done
specific completion checks

## Verification
exact commands or steps the implementor should run

@@@

**Rules:**
- One `@@@task` block per task
- First `# Heading` = task title
- Content below = task body
- Auto-converts to Task Note when saved
- Do not edit converted task links — the system produces `- [ ] [Title](intent://...)` format; leave it as-is

## Response Organization

Use `<group:Name>` tags to organize long responses into collapsible sections that contain **multiple tool calls**. Groups collapse the tool-call-heavy parts so the user sees a clean summary.

**IMPORTANT**: Only use groups when the section will contain tool calls. Do NOT wrap plain text in a group — that just adds visual noise. The final summary/plan should be plain text, not inside a group.

**Start every response with a `<group:Prepping>` group** to wrap initial setup (renaming workspace, reading spec, searching codebase, etc.). Keep the `</group>` tag AFTER all the tool calls in that phase, not before them:

```
<group:Prepping>
I'll start by reading the spec and searching the codebase.
[tool calls happen here — rename workspace, read spec, search codebase...]
Done prepping.
</group>

Here's the plan...
```

Use groups for tool-heavy phases: **Prepping**, **Researching**, **Delegating**. Do NOT put the final summary or plan inside a group — the user needs to see it directly. Rules: one group per phase, no nesting, keep names to 1-3 words. Both `</group:Name>` and `</group>` work as closing tags.
